question: Tetanospasmin causes flaccid paralysis by blocking acetylcholine release at the neuromuscular junction, similar to botulinum toxin.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is false. Tetanospasmin causes SPASTIC paralysis (not flaccid). It travels retrograde to spinal cord inhibitory interneurones where it cleaves synaptobrevin, blocking GABA/glycine release — resulting in loss of inhibition and spasm. Botulinum toxin acts at the NMJ blocking ACh, causing flaccid paralysis.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this statement is false. Tetanospasmin causes SPASTIC paralysis by cleaving synaptobrevin (VAMP) in INHIBITORY interneurones, blocking GABA and glycine release. Loss of inhibition produces unopposed excitation and muscle spasm. Botulinum toxin is the one that causes flaccid paralysis by blocking ACh release at the NMJ.
